Maya Chen: Heads-up: noticed a p95 latency spike on /v1/generate for tier=prod starting ~07:10UTC after we pushed the new dynamic token-budget heuristic to canary.
Jason Patel: I saw alerts too. Only affecting a subset of routes? numbers?
Maya Chen: Yes. routes with long-context (>=1024) and small token budgets for interactive tier. p95 jumped from ~120ms -> 370ms on those routes, p50 fine. CPU/GPU look nominal.
Tony R.: Could be batching behavior: small budgets -> more microbatches (?) -> kernel switch thrash. Did profiling run yet?
Liu Zhao: Running perf profile now. Quick grep of logs shows a lot more KV cache miss penalties around the same timeframe.
canary-bot: [deploy] Dynamic token-budget heuristic v2 deployed to canary pool (canary-7). Roll ID: r-2026-03-18-07:08
Nina_sre_bot: alert: p95_guideline_exceeded on /v1/generate tier=prod route=chat-ia interactive
Maya Chen: Attaching quick profiler snapshots (summaries):
- flame: https://profiler.internal/shot/1789994433/flame (sample shows long tail in attention_kernel_switch)
- topo: kernel selection count: attention_fast: 2000 -> 2100, attention_fallback: 40 -> 420
Jason Patel: Interesting: fallback kernel invocations x10. That fallback has higher setup cost and doesn't mesh well with our batching pool.
Tony R.: That explains p50 stable (short requests still on fast kernel) and p95 blowing up for those with fallback.
Liu Zhao: KV cache misses amplified the problem because fallback kernel forces KV reshuffle resulting in more memory copies. I see memcopy spikes in GPU profiler:

```
GPU copy (H2D): 14.7ms -> 80.2ms
KV-load-latency avg: 0.9ms -> 6.1ms
```
Maya Chen: Root cause hypothesis: the new token-budget heuristic reduced per-request token budget aggressively for interactive tier; that changed effective sequence length distribution used by kernel selection AND increased fragmentation in batch formation. Kernel selector decided fallback for mixed batches.
Jason Patel: So two failure modes: 1) token budgets -> skewed seq lengths -> wrong kernel chosen, 2) queue policy mixes long KV-miss requests into the same microbatch as short requests, causing fallback.
Tony R.: Repro steps on dev: run a mixed workload (60% short prompts w/ cache hits, 40% long w/ cold KV) and enable v2 heuristic. I can reproduce p95 regression locally with similar profiler traces.
Maya Chen: For mitigation, propose immediate canary rollback for the heuristic and a short-term patch to batching policy: prefer homogeneous batches by token-budget bucket and avoid mixing requests with different kernel affinity.
Liu Zhao: Agreed. Also propose adding a per-route hard cap for max_batch_size when route historically has KV misses > 5% to avoid large cross-traffic batches. That will reduce serialization penalties.
Jason Patel: Small patch candidates:
- rollback canary (quick)
- change scheduler: prefer same-kernel affinity within microbatch (heuristic: kernel_score delta < 0.15)
- route config: token_budget_min=16 for interactive to avoid ultra-small budgets triggering fallback
- metric: kernel_fallback_rate per route
Tony R.: I'll open a PR for scheduler affinity and a canary rollback doc.
canary-bot: [action] Rolling back r-2026-03-18-07:08 from canary-7 -> scheduled
Maya Chen: Quick experiments I'd like:
1) Run scheduler-affinity in canary with route-filter=chat-ia only (observe p95)
2) Add KV-miss indicator to batcher to deprioritize stale-key requests during batch forming
3) Adjust kernel selection threshold to favor fast kernel if batch has > 70% fast-affinity requests
Liu Zhao: For (2) we can surface a header kv_warm: true/false based on LRU probe. Then batcher can prefer kv_warm first.
Jason Patel: Also add lightweight sampling to log batch composition: token_budget, seq_len, kernel_affinity, kv_warm. That will help confirm mixing hypothesis.
Maya Chen: Action items:
- Tony: PR for rollback and scheduler affinity (ETA 2h)
- Jason: Add batch composition sampling metric and dashboard (ETA EOD)
- Liu: Add kv_warm probe + per-route max_batch config (ETA 1d)
- Me: Coordinate canary run and monitor p95 (I'll own the canary run)
Tony R.: PR opened: https://git.internal/r/infra/batcher/pulls/312
Tony R.: Implemented scheduler affinity: pseudo-snippet in PR description:
```
if kernel_score_variance(batch) > 0.15:
  split_batch_by_affinity()
else:
  keep_batch()
```
Jason Patel: Sampling logs example (line):
```
batch_id=bb-233 token_budget=[32,8,32] seq_lens=[24,512,18] kernel_affinity=[fast,fallback,fast] kv_warm=[1,0,1]
```
Liu Zhao: For the per-route cap, I'm proposing: chat-ia.max_batch=8 (was 16), chat-bot.max_batch=12
Maya Chen: After Tony's rollback and quick scheduler-affinity patch, I see canary p95 drop back to baseline within 20m. Will validate over next 2h.
canary-bot: [deploy] scheduler-affinity patch deployed to canary-7. Roll ID: r-2026-03-18-09:12
Maya Chen: Observed: fallback kernel rate down 6x, KV-memcopy spikes reduced, p95 back near 140ms on affected routes. Good.
Jason Patel: Follow-ups:
- longer-term: kernel selector should accept batch-level statistics, not per-request. Need a small redesign so the choice is based on batch histogram instead of per-request.
- e2e test: synthetic mixed workload that asserts p95 < 200ms at canary scale.
Liu Zhao: Also file perf regression ticket with attached flamegraphs and memcopy traces. I'll include recommended per-route defaults.
Maya Chen: I'll write a short postmortem and schedule a 30m sync to decide whether to roll changes into stable after tests. Thanks for the quick turnaround :thumbsup:
Nina_sre_bot: incident: created INC-2026-0318-02 -> p95-surge-dynamic-token-budget
Maya Chen: Meeting invite sent for 10:30 UTC — include runtime + infra + sres.
